In a finite deterministic search model, an integer budget starts at B >= 0. Each transition reduces budget by exactly one; budget is never replenished and no transition is allowed at zero.

After k transitions the budget is B-k by induction. Nonnegativity implies k <= B, so termination occurs within B transitions. The theorem makes no claim about optimality or empirical discovery success.
